text:
lee: Client reported a 400 on tool/function call when the args JSON contains percent-encoded CRLF sequences and a trailing comma. Attaching the payload they pasted.

lee: ```json
{
  "tool": "pdf-extract",
  "args": "{\"path\":\"C:%5C%5Creports%5C%5Cfile%2520name.pdf%5Cr%5Cn\",\"pages\": [1,2,],} "
}
```

support-bot: Ticket #7892 created (severity: P2). Assigned to @jess.

jess: Can you confirm the raw HTTP body and Content-Type header the client sends? UI screenshots can mask encoding.

client-app: We send Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8. Our stack URL-encodes file paths as a legacy behavior. Raw body we receive from our frontend (what we forward):

client-app: ```
POST /v1/toolcall HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{
  "tool": "pdf-extract",
  "args": "{\"path\":\"C:%5C%5Creports%5C%5Cfile%2520name.pdf%5Cr%5Cn\",\"pages\": [1,2,],}"
}
```

jess: Repro: curl with the same body -> 400 response body: {"error":"Invalid tool args: Unexpected token % in JSON at position 15"}. Our parser tries to parse the `args` value as JSON string, sees percent sign and fails.

samir: Two things: the payload has a trailing comma in the array (`[1,2,]`) which our strict JSON validator rejects, and the `args` string is URL-encoded (e.g. `%5Cr%5Cn` / `%0D%0A`) inside a JSON string. We only decode URL-encoded bodies for `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, not for `application/json`. Looks like their client double-encoded or pre-encoded the path string.

lee: Customer is asking for a quick workaround—can we accept lenient parsing server-side? Concern about silently accepting malformed input.

samir: Lenient parsing carries risks (injection, ambiguity). Short-term: improve error to be actionable: detect percent-encoded sequences inside JSON string fields and return 400 with message: `percent-encoded sequences detected inside JSON string: please send raw JSON or set Content-Type to application/x-www-form-urlencoded if sending urlencoded payload` and include link to docs. That way it's clear.

jess: I can open a tiny PR to enhance the validator error classification and add a hint for percent-encoding + trailing-comma diagnostics. For immediate customer help, advise them to un-URL-encode their string before sending or to send the args object as a nested JSON object (not a string). Example client curl to work: 

jess: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/toolcall \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"tool":"pdf-extract","args":{"path":"C:\\reports\\file name.pdf","pages":[1,2]}}'
```

client-app: We'll try sending raw JSON like that and report back. Thanks.

lee: :thumbsup: I'll log the customer follow-up.

samir: I'll add a short note in the incident log to track if we see this pattern from other clients (SDKs that url-encode strings).
